An admin who enters 'example.com/allowed-path' gets the whole host whitelisted — silent path dropping is a real, specific scope/security tradeoff a maintainer should weigh. However, host-level allow-listing matches the replaced SiteSetting behavior (URI(h).host comparison in site_setting.rb), so this is a design/scope concern, not a behavior regression, hence not a bug.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows EmbeddableHost normalizes stored entries to effectively just the domain (before_validation strips scheme and any path in app/models/embeddable_host.rb) and authorization checks only URI(host).host in record_for_host/host_allowed?, so embeds are allowed based solely on hostname, with no ability to scope to a specific path (and ports are ignored by using uri.host). This matches the finding as a security/scope concern, but it’s not clearly a defect introduced here since the previous SiteSetting-based implementation also primarily compared by host and did not support path scoping either.
